questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Oslo because I wanted to stay in the Nordic region, study in beautiful nature similar to Bornholm, and take courses in genetics that fit my academic interests. The combination of strong academics, nature, and being close to my family was crucial for my choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find most of the information I needed upon arrival. The only part that was difficult was getting details about my courses, since the final confirmation came quite late.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received clear guidance from the university through their welcome materials, and I could always call the student help service if I had questions. They were very helpful and made the arrival process easier.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to find off-campus housing, but it’s important to start early because rooms are in high demand. I recommend checking student housing platforms and being flexible with location, since public transport in Oslo works very well.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Future exchange students should know that living off campus in Oslo is safe and convenient, but it can be expensive. Public transport is reliable and makes it easy to get around, so living a bit outside the city center works well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process at the University of Oslo was straightforward. I activated my student account online, completed the required forms in the student portal, and attended the welcome day where everything was explained. The only challenging part was that course confirmations came quite late.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was good support available. I could call the student help service whenever I had questions, and they guided me through practical steps and general information.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was fully successful in registering for the classes I wanted, and I got all the courses I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My advice is to stay patient and check the student portal regularly, because course confirmations can come late. If anything is unclear, contact the student help service — they respond quickly and are very helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was as expected. They were academically challenging but manageable, and the teachers explained the material clearly. The workload was reasonable and fit well with my background in molecular biomedicine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style at the University of Oslo was similar to UCPH, with a mix of lectures and independent study. The structure was a bit more relaxed, and the teachers were very approachable. There was also a strong focus on student participation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I was enrolled in the following courses during my first semester:
• General Toxicology
• Human Physiology
• Bioinformatics for Molecular Biology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all the courses I took, because they complemented each other well, and the exam schedule and teaching plan were very well aligned. This made the semester both manageable and enjoyable.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had an unexpected one-time cost of DKK 1,500 to have the furniture removed from the apartment.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than I expected, while public transport was cheaper and very cost-effective.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many activities available, including cultural events, student clubs, sports facilities at SiO Athletica, and social gatherings organized by student associations. It was easy to join both athletic and social activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend travelling around Norway, especially going to places like Stavanger, and doing lots of hikes. The nature is amazing, and hiking is a great way to experience the country and spend time with other students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend exploring Norway’s nature on weekends — hiking, visiting fjords, or taking short trips to cities like Stavanger. It’s a great way to relax and experience the country beyond campus.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy to adjust to the local culture, as Norwegians are friendly and the lifestyle is very similar to Denmark. This made the transition smooth and comfortable.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I don’t have specific tips for socializing with local students, as I went on exchange with my partner and spent most of my free time with him.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I especially appreciated the calm atmosphere, the closeness to nature, and the strong focus on work–life balance.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1.	Be prepared for higher food prices, but enjoy that public transport is cheap and reliable.
	2.	Stay patient with course registration, as confirmations can come late.
	3.	Use your weekends to explore nature — hiking is one of the best parts of living in Norway.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It’s helpful to plan a budget before arriving, as small daily expenses can add up. Also, make use of the university’s support services — they are very responsive and make the whole experience smoother. And don’t miss the chance to travel and hike; it’s one of the biggest advantages of studying in Norway.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was the hikes. Exploring Norway’s nature made the whole stay unforgettable.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during the exchange was the high food prices, which made budgeting more difficult than expected.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
